name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
description: The RTX 5090 is the fastest gaming GPU you can buy: 32 GB of GDDR7 and 21,760 CUDA cores for 4K, but it draws 575 W and costs $2,000 or more.
quick: NVIDIA's flagship pairs 32 GB of GDDR7 on a 512-bit bus with 21,760 CUDA cores. It is rated for 575 W, and NVIDIA recommends a 1,000 W power supply.
bestFor: 4K high-refresh gaming, path tracing and local AI work that needs 32 GB of VRAM
skipIf: you game at 1440p or your budget stops below $1,500
verdict: The RTX 5090 is the fastest consumer graphics card on sale, and independent reviews put it roughly 25–35% ahead of the RTX 4090 at 4K. Its 32 GB of GDDR7 on a 512-bit bus delivers 1,792 GB/s of bandwidth, which pays off in path-traced games at 4K and in local AI models that will not fit in 16 GB.

The trade-off is cost and power. NVIDIA rates the card at 575 W and recommends a 1,000 W power supply, and street prices of $2,000 to $2,700 sit above the $1,999 launch price. That is about twice the price of an [RTX 5080](/gear/rtx-5080/) for a performance gap that is large at 4K but nowhere near double. Owners have also reported melted 16-pin connectors, so a fully seated native 12V-2x6 cable from an ATX 3.1 power supply matters more here than on any other card.

There is no consumer step-up; this is the top of NVIDIA's range. The closest rival is a used RTX 4090, which lacks Multi Frame Generation and has 24 GB but can cost far less if you find a clean one. AMD has nothing in this class, since the RX 9070 XT targets the RTX 5070 Ti. Buy the 5090 for 4K at 144 Hz or more, path tracing with every setting on, or AI work. At 1440p it is mostly paying for headroom you will not see.

Overkill below 4K

extra.heading: Drivers and Updates
body: NVIDIA releases Game Ready drivers once or twice a month, timed to major game launches. The NVIDIA App handles updates and includes DLSS Override, which can apply the newer transformer upscaling model or Multi Frame Generation in supported games without waiting for a patch.

Do a clean install when moving from an older GeForce card with years of saved profiles, or when an update brings crashes or black screens. If the previous card was AMD or Intel, remove its driver with Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) in Safe Mode first. After any driver or hardware change, check that the 16-pin plug is still fully seated with no visible gap.

faqs.q: What power supply does the RTX 5090 need?
faqs.a: NVIDIA recommends at least 1,000 W. Choose an ATX 3.1 unit with a native 12V-2x6 cable, such as the [Corsair RM1000x](/gear/corsair-rm1000x/), rather than relying on the multi-plug adapter.

faqs.q: Is the RTX 5090 worth it over the RTX 4090?
faqs.a: Only if you are buying new. Independent reviews show about 25–35% more 4K performance plus Multi Frame Generation, but a used RTX 4090 at a fair price is still an excellent 4K card.

faqs.q: Will the RTX 5090 fit in my case?
faqs.a: Check before you order. The Founders Edition is a two-slot card, but many partner models are much thicker and longer, so measure GPU length and slot clearance first.

faqs.q: Does the RTX 5090 lose performance on PCIe 4.0?
faqs.a: Only a little. Independent reviews show a loss of a few percent at most when it runs at PCIe 4.0 x16 instead of PCIe 5.0 x16.

name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080
description: The RTX 5080 is a strong 4K and 1440p card with 16 GB of GDDR7 at 360 W, but at $1,000 to $1,300 it is a small step over the RTX 5070 Ti for its price.
quick: The RTX 5080 is NVIDIA's second-tier Blackwell card, with 10,752 CUDA cores and 16 GB of GDDR7 on a 256-bit bus. It is rated for 360 W, and NVIDIA recommends an 850 W power supply.
bestFor: high-refresh 1440p and 4K with DLSS when an RTX 5090 is out of reach
skipIf: you can find an RTX 5070 Ti near $750, which gets most of the way there for far less
verdict: The RTX 5080 is the fastest card NVIDIA sells below the 5090, but it is a smaller generational jump than buyers hoped for. Independent reviews put it roughly 10–15% ahead of the RTX 4080 Super and still behind the RTX 4090 in most games. With 10,752 CUDA cores, 16 GB of GDDR7 and 960 GB/s of bandwidth, it handles 4K with DLSS and very high frame rates at 1440p.

The main problem is the card below it. The [RTX 5070 Ti](/gear/rtx-5070-ti/) has the same 256-bit bus and the same 16 GB, and independent reviews typically put the 5080 only about 15% ahead. Yet street prices of $1,000 to $1,300 against $750 to $900 make the 5080 30–45% more expensive. Its 16 GB is enough for current games but leaves less room for 4K path tracing over the next few years than the 5090's 32 GB.

The step-up is the [RTX 5090](/gear/rtx-5090/), at roughly double the price. The closest rival is a used RTX 4090 near the same money, with 24 GB and a little more raw speed but no Multi Frame Generation. AMD has no RX 9000 card at this tier. On the plus side, 360 W runs comfortably on an 850 W Gold unit, and reviewers found unusually large overclocking headroom. Buy the 5080 if the 5070 Ti is out of stock near its launch price, or if you want the extra margin at 4K and accept paying for it.

cons: Small gain over the RTX 4080 Super

body: The RTX 5080 shares its driver branch with every RTX 50 card. Drivers in early 2025 drew widely reported black-screen and stability complaints, and later releases fixed most of them, so start any new build on the latest Game Ready driver rather than the one on the box or disc.

If you replaced an older GeForce card, the existing driver usually keeps working, but a clean install clears old profiles and overclock settings that can cause odd behavior. Save DDU in Safe Mode for a move from AMD or Intel, or for crashes that a normal clean install does not fix.

faqs.q: Is the RTX 5080 faster than the RTX 4090?
faqs.a: No. Independent reviews put the RTX 4090 ahead in most games at 4K, though the 5080 can show higher frame rates in games that use Multi Frame Generation, which the 4090 lacks.

faqs.q: What power supply does the RTX 5080 need?
faqs.a: NVIDIA recommends 850 W. A quality 850 W Gold unit with a native 12V-2x6 cable, such as the [Corsair RM850x](/gear/corsair-rm850x/), covers the card and a high-end CPU.

faqs.q: Should I buy the RTX 5080 or the RTX 5070 Ti?
faqs.a: For most buyers, the RTX 5070 Ti. It has the same 16 GB and 256-bit bus, and the roughly 15% speed gap rarely justifies paying $250 or more extra.

faqs.q: Is 16 GB of VRAM enough for 4K?
faqs.a: Yes for current games with DLSS. Heavy path-traced games at maximum settings can use most of it, so 16 GB is adequate rather than generous for a card at this price.

name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
description: The RTX 5070 Ti is the best 16 GB NVIDIA card for 1440p and 4K: 8,960 CUDA cores at 300 W, close to an RTX 4080, for $750 to $900 at street prices.
quick: The RTX 5070 Ti uses a cut-down RTX 5080 chip with 8,960 CUDA cores and the same 16 GB of GDDR7 on a 256-bit bus. NVIDIA rates it at 300 W and recommends a 750 W power supply.
bestFor: high-refresh 1440p and 4K with DLSS for under $900
skipIf: you mostly play raster games and an RX 9070 XT costs $100 or more less
verdict: The RTX 5070 Ti is the NVIDIA card most high-end buyers should pick. It keeps the RTX 5080's 256-bit bus and 16 GB of GDDR7 at 896 GB/s, and independent reviews place it close to the last-generation RTX 4080. That makes it a very high-refresh 1440p card and a solid 4K card once DLSS upscaling is on.

Its main rival is the [RX 9070 XT](/gear/rx-9070-xt/). The two trade blows in raster games, and the AMD card usually costs $100 to $150 less. The 5070 Ti pulls ahead in heavy ray tracing and path tracing, and DLSS 4 is supported in far more games than FSR 4. If you play Cyberpunk 2077 or Alan Wake 2 with path tracing, or use CUDA apps for rendering or AI, the premium is easy to justify. For raster-only gaming it is harder to defend.

The step-up is the [RTX 5080](/gear/rtx-5080/), about 15% faster for 30–45% more money, which is poor value. One tier down, the RTX 5070 saves around $200 but drops to 12 GB on a 192-bit bus. At 300 W, the 5070 Ti runs on a 750 W Gold power supply, and most partner cards use a single 16-pin connector. Look for models near the $749 launch price; above $900 the case for it weakens quickly against the cheaper AMD card.

No Founders Edition, so prices vary widely by model

Choose a clean installation when you upgrade from an RTX 20 or 30 series card and notice stutter or crashes after the swap. The NVIDIA App's custom install handles that without a separate tool; keep DDU for brand switches or stubborn problems.

faqs.q: Is the RTX 5070 Ti good for 4K?
faqs.a: Yes, with DLSS. It runs most games at 4K and high settings with upscaling on, and its 16 GB of VRAM leaves room for high-resolution textures.

faqs.q: RTX 5070 Ti or RX 9070 XT?
faqs.a: Pick the RTX 5070 Ti for ray tracing, DLSS and CUDA apps; pick the RX 9070 XT if you mostly play raster games and want to save $100 or more. Raster performance is close in independent reviews.

faqs.q: What power supply does the RTX 5070 Ti need?
faqs.a: NVIDIA recommends 750 W. A Gold unit with a native 12V-2x6 cable, such as the [Corsair RM750e](/gear/corsair-rm750e/), is a clean fit with no adapter.

name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070
description: The RTX 5070 is the best value NVIDIA card for 1440p: roughly RTX 4070 Super speed, DLSS 4 and 250 W for $550 to $650, held back by its 12 GB of VRAM.
quick: The RTX 5070 has 6,144 CUDA cores and 12 GB of GDDR7 on a 192-bit bus. NVIDIA rates it at 250 W and recommends a 650 W power supply.
bestFor: 1440p gaming with DLSS and ray tracing on a mid-range budget
skipIf: you plan to keep the card four or more years at maximum textures, where 16 GB is safer
verdict: The RTX 5070 is the card to beat for 1440p if you want NVIDIA features at a mid-range price. Independent reviews show it roughly matching the RTX 4070 Super, and with 6,144 CUDA cores, 672 GB/s of bandwidth and DLSS 4, it runs most games at 1440p and high settings at high refresh rates. NVIDIA's launch claim of RTX 4090 performance relied on Multi Frame Generation and does not reflect native speed.

The trade-off is 12 GB of VRAM. That is enough for 1440p today, but a growing list of games at maximum textures with ray tracing can fill it, and 16 GB cards sell for about the same money. The [RX 9070](/gear/rx-9070/) is the closest rival: 16 GB, slightly faster in raster in most independent reviews and rated at 220 W, though it trails in ray tracing and FSR 4 is in fewer games than DLSS.

The step-up is the [RTX 5070 Ti](/gear/rtx-5070-ti/), which adds 4 GB and a 256-bit bus for about $200 more. At 250 W, the 5070 runs on a 650 W power supply, and the two-slot Founders Edition suits compact cases. Owners moving up from an RTX 3060 or RTX 2070 class card will see a large jump at 1440p. Buy it at or near $550 for a DLSS-first 1440p build. Above $650, the 16 GB alternatives make more sense.

A clean installation is worth doing when the 5070 replaces a much older GeForce card or after a driver update that causes crashes. Coming from a Radeon card, run DDU in Safe Mode to remove AMD's driver before installing NVIDIA's.

faqs.q: Is 12 GB of VRAM enough for 1440p?
faqs.a: For most games, yes. A few demanding titles at maximum textures with ray tracing can exceed it, so drop texture quality one step if you see stutter.

faqs.q: Is the RTX 5070 as fast as an RTX 4090?
faqs.a: No. NVIDIA's claim relied on 4x Multi Frame Generation. In native rendering, independent reviews put it near the RTX 4070 Super, far below the 4090.

faqs.q: RTX 5070 or RX 9070?
faqs.a: Pick the RTX 5070 for DLSS, ray tracing and CUDA apps. Pick the RX 9070 for 16 GB of VRAM, slightly better raster speed and lower power draw.

name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB
description: The RTX 5060 Ti 16GB is a sound 1080p and 1440p card: 16 GB of GDDR7 at 180 W with DLSS 4, though its PCIe 5.0 x8 link costs a little on older boards.
quick: The RTX 5060 Ti 16GB has 4,608 CUDA cores and 16 GB of GDDR7 on a 128-bit bus. It is rated at 180 W and uses an eight-lane PCIe 5.0 link.
bestFor: 1080p and 1440p gamers who want 16 GB and DLSS for under $500
skipIf: your board is PCIe 3.0 and an RX 9060 XT 16GB with a full x16 link costs $50 to $80 less
verdict: The RTX 5060 Ti 16GB is the cheapest NVIDIA card with enough memory to age well. Its 16 GB of GDDR7 avoids the texture limits that hit 8 GB cards, and 4,608 CUDA cores with 448 GB/s of bandwidth make it a strong 1080p card and a capable 1440p one with DLSS. Independent reviews show a modest gain over the RTX 4060 Ti it replaces rather than a generational leap.

The catch is its PCIe 5.0 x8 interface. On a PCIe 4.0 or 5.0 board that is plenty, but in a PCIe 3.0 slot, such as a B450 board with a Ryzen 5 2600, the available bandwidth drops again and independent reviews show small losses that grow when VRAM runs short. The 16 GB model suffers far less from this than the 8 GB version, one more reason to skip the 8 GB card entirely.

The closest rival is the [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/): similar raster speed in independent reviews, a full x16 link and usually $50 to $80 less. The 5060 Ti wins on ray tracing, DLSS game support and CUDA software. The step-up is the [RTX 5070](/gear/rtx-5070/), clearly faster for roughly $120 to $170 more but with 12 GB. At 180 W, the 5060 Ti suits small cases and modest power supplies, and its performance per watt is among the best in this price class.

extra.heading: Drivers and Updates
body: The RTX 5060 Ti uses the same Game Ready driver as the rest of the RTX 50 series, so fixes for new games reach it on the same day as the flagships. Many buyers install it in an older PC, so update the motherboard chipset driver as well.

Upgrading from an RTX 2060 or a GTX 16-series card, a normal install over the old driver usually works; pick a clean installation if games crash after the swap. If the old card was a Radeon, run DDU in Safe Mode first. On older boards, also enable Resizable BAR in the BIOS, which may need a BIOS update on B450 and similar boards.

faqs.q: Does the RTX 5060 Ti work on PCIe 3.0?
faqs.a: Yes, with a small performance loss. It uses eight lanes, so a PCIe 3.0 slot gives it a quarter of the bandwidth it gets on a PCIe 5.0 board. The 16 GB model is affected far less than the 8 GB one because it rarely runs out of VRAM.

faqs.q: Should I buy the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB or 8GB?
faqs.a: Get the 16 GB model. The 8 GB version costs less but runs out of memory in several current games at high textures, even at 1080p.

faqs.q: Is the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB good for 1440p?
faqs.a: Yes, at medium to high settings with DLSS on. For maximum settings at high refresh rates, step up to an RTX 5070 or RX 9070.

name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060
description: The RTX 5060 is a capable 1080p card at $300 to $330 with DLSS 4 and a 145 W draw, but its 8 GB of VRAM already forces lower textures in some new games.
quick: The RTX 5060 has 3,840 CUDA cores and 8 GB of GDDR7 on a 128-bit bus. It is rated at 145 W and runs on an eight-lane PCIe 5.0 link.
bestFor: 1080p esports and older games on a tight budget, especially in small or low-power builds
skipIf: you play new AAA games at high textures or can stretch to a 16 GB card
verdict: The RTX 5060 is a quick 1080p card held back by its memory. Independent reviews put it around 20% ahead of the RTX 4060, and with 3,840 CUDA cores, GDDR7 at 448 GB/s and DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation, it runs esports titles at very high frame rates and most AAA games at 1080p medium to high settings.

The problem is 8 GB of VRAM. Several recent games at high or ultra textures exceed 8 GB even at 1080p, and frame generation itself needs extra memory. When the card runs out, frame pacing suffers badly, and on a PCIe 3.0 board the x8 link makes that spillover worse. Lowering textures works around it, but that is a compromise to accept on a new $300 card.

The closest rivals are the [Arc B580](/gear/arc-b580/), which offers 12 GB for less money but carries CPU-overhead caveats on older processors, and the [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/), which costs about $50 to $70 more and doubles the memory. That Radeon card, or the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, is the step-up most buyers should take. The RTX 5060 still makes sense in a compact, low-power build, where 145 W is easy to feed, or for players who stick to competitive shooters that never touch the 8 GB limit.

In an older PCIe 3.0 system, enable Resizable BAR in the BIOS if the board offers it and update the chipset driver. A clean installation through the NVIDIA App is enough when upgrading from an older GeForce card; use DDU in Safe Mode when the previous card was AMD or Intel.

faqs.q: Is 8 GB of VRAM enough in 2026?
faqs.a: For esports and older games, yes. For new AAA releases at high textures, often not, so lower texture quality to stay within 8 GB and avoid stutter.

faqs.q: RTX 5060 or Arc B580?
faqs.a: With a recent CPU like a Ryzen 5 7600, the B580's 12 GB makes it the better AAA card. With an older CPU such as a Ryzen 5 2600 or 3600, the RTX 5060 avoids the B580's driver overhead.

faqs.q: What power supply does the RTX 5060 need?
faqs.a: A quality 450 to 550 W unit is plenty for the 145 W card and a mainstream CPU. Most models use one 8-pin PCIe connector, so check that your PSU has a spare lead.

name: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT
description: The RX 9070 XT is the best value high-end card: 16 GB, raster speed close to an RTX 5070 Ti and FSR 4 for $600 to $730, at the cost of a 304 W power draw.
quick: AMD's top RDNA 4 card has 64 compute units (4,096 stream processors) and 16 GB of GDDR6 on a 256-bit bus. AMD rates it at 304 W, and most partner cards use standard 8-pin connectors.
bestFor: 1440p high-refresh and 4K raster gaming for well under RTX 5070 Ti money
skipIf: path tracing, CUDA apps or the widest upscaler support matter more to you than price
verdict: The RX 9070 XT is the best value high-end graphics card for most gamers. Independent reviews show it trading blows with the [RTX 5070 Ti](/gear/rtx-5070-ti/) in raster games, and its 16 GB of GDDR6 on a 256-bit bus gives it room for 4K textures. At $600 to $730, it usually costs $100 to $200 less than the NVIDIA card.

RDNA 4 also fixed two long-standing AMD weaknesses. Ray tracing is much improved over the RX 7000 series, though the 5070 Ti still leads in heavy path tracing. FSR 4 is a machine-learning upscaler with image quality much closer to DLSS than FSR 3, and AMD Software can upgrade many FSR 3.1 games to FSR 4. The catch is coverage: DLSS still appears in many more games.

The trade-off is power. At 304 W, and more on factory-overclocked models, it draws more than the 5070 Ti for similar raster speed, so plan for a 750 W unit. Most cards use two or three 8-pin plugs instead of a 16-pin connector, which suits older power supplies. The step-down is the [RX 9070](/gear/rx-9070/), roughly 10–15% slower at 220 W; there is no faster RDNA 4 card above it. Buy the XT near $600 for 1440p or 4K raster gaming. Above $730, the 5070 Ti becomes the better deal.

extra.heading: Drivers and Updates
body: AMD releases Adrenalin drivers about monthly, with optional builds in between for big game launches. Adrenalin also holds the FSR 4 upgrade setting that swaps FSR 3.1 for FSR 4 in supported games, and new drivers keep adding titles to that list.

Choose Factory Reset in the installer when moving from an older Radeon card, or when a game crashes after an update. Coming from an NVIDIA card, remove the GeForce driver with DDU in Safe Mode first, so old services and control panels do not linger.

Launch AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition from the Start menu or the system tray, or press Alt+R.
Check for updates
On the Home tab, click Check for Updates. Recommended drivers are WHQL-certified; Optional drivers arrive sooner with fixes for new games.
Install
Download the update and run it. For a clean install, tick Factory Reset in the installer, which removes old driver files and settings first.
Restart
Reboot, then reapply any tuning profile or per-game settings, since a Factory Reset clears them.

faqs.q: RX 9070 XT or RTX 5070 Ti?
faqs.a: For raster gaming and value, the RX 9070 XT. For path tracing, DLSS game support and CUDA software, the RTX 5070 Ti. Raster speed is close in independent reviews.

faqs.q: Does FSR 4 work on older Radeon cards?
faqs.a: AMD built FSR 4 for RX 9000 series cards and their RDNA 4 AI hardware. Older Radeon cards use FSR 3.1, which looks noticeably softer in motion.

faqs.q: What power supply does the RX 9070 XT need?
faqs.a: Plan on 750 W. A Gold unit with three separate PCIe 8-pin leads covers even factory-overclocked models, which draw more than the 304 W reference rating.

faqs.q: Is the RX 9070 XT good for 4K?
faqs.a: Yes for most games at high settings with FSR upscaling, and its 16 GB handles 4K textures. In heavy ray tracing at 4K, it falls further behind NVIDIA.

name: AMD Radeon RX 9070
description: The RX 9070 is the most efficient 16 GB card for 1440p: 220 W, raster speed a little above the RTX 5070, and FSR 4, for $550 to $620 at street prices.
quick: The RX 9070 uses the same chip as the RX 9070 XT with 56 compute units (3,584 stream processors) and the full 16 GB of GDDR6 on a 256-bit bus. AMD rates it at 220 W.
bestFor: 1440p gamers who want 16 GB and low power draw at an RTX 5070 price
skipIf: the RX 9070 XT is within $50, where its extra speed is the better buy
verdict: The RX 9070 is the efficient one in AMD's lineup. It keeps the full 16 GB and 256-bit bus of the [RX 9070 XT](/gear/rx-9070-xt/), drops to 56 compute units and cuts board power from 304 W to 220 W. Independent reviews show it roughly 10–15% behind the XT and slightly ahead of the [RTX 5070](/gear/rtx-5070/) in raster games, which makes it one of the best performance-per-watt cards of this generation.

Against the RTX 5070, the RX 9070 brings 4 GB more VRAM and lower power at a similar price. The NVIDIA card is still better at heavy ray tracing, and DLSS 4 appears in many more games than FSR 4. If your library leans on path-traced showcases, the 5070 has the edge. For almost everything else, the extra memory makes the 9070 the safer card to keep for several years.

The awkward part is AMD's own pricing. The XT often costs only $50 to $100 more, and at that gap the faster card gives more performance per dollar. The 9070 makes most sense in quiet or small-form-factor builds, or when your current power supply is a 650 W unit you would rather not replace. Owners report that many models run cool and quiet, and Adrenalin's tuning page makes undervolting simple.

verdict: The RX 9060 XT 16GB is the budget card to buy right now. For $350 to $400, it pairs 16 GB of GDDR6 with 32 RDNA 4 compute units and FSR 4, and independent reviews put it within a few percent of the [RTX 5060 Ti 16GB](/gear/rtx-5060-ti-16gb/) in raster games. That makes it a high-settings 1080p card and a capable 1440p one with upscaling.

Its less obvious advantage is the full PCIe 5.0 x16 link. NVIDIA's 5060-class cards use eight lanes, which costs a little on PCIe 3.0 boards; the 9060 XT keeps all 16, so it loses less in an older B450 system with a Ryzen 5 2600 or 3600. At about 160 W, it also runs on modest power supplies and fits small cases.

The trade-offs are ray tracing and upscaler coverage. NVIDIA still leads in heavy ray tracing, and FSR 4 appears in fewer games than DLSS 4. The 128-bit bus also limits it at higher resolutions, so maximum settings at 1440p are a stretch. Avoid the 8 GB version, which shares the name but hits memory limits in new games. The step-up is the [RX 9070](/gear/rx-9070/), much faster with a 256-bit bus for roughly $200 more. For most 1080p players, this card is the better use of the money.

name: Intel Arc B580
description: The Arc B580 is a strong value pick at $250 to $290 with 12 GB of VRAM and XeSS 2, but CPU overhead hurts it on older chips like the Ryzen 5 2600 or 3600.
quick: Intel's Battlemage card has 20 Xe2 cores and 12 GB of GDDR6 on a 192-bit bus. It is rated at 190 W, uses a PCIe 4.0 x8 link and requires Resizable BAR.

verdict: The Arc B580 offers more VRAM per dollar than any other current card: 12 GB of GDDR6 on a 192-bit bus for $250 to $290. Paired with a fast, recent CPU, independent reviews show it ahead of the RTX 4060 at 1080p and 1440p, and XeSS 2 adds AI upscaling and frame generation in supported games.

The big caveat is CPU overhead. Independent reviews widely reported that Intel's driver leans harder on the processor than AMD's or NVIDIA's, so with older chips like the Ryzen 5 2600 or 3600 the B580 can lose a large share of its performance and fall behind cheaper cards. It also requires Resizable BAR, which many older boards gained only through a BIOS update, and its PCIe 4.0 x8 link loses a little more on PCIe 3.0 slots. Driver quality has improved steadily, but older and less popular games remain less consistent than on AMD or NVIDIA.

The closest rival is the [RTX 5060](/gear/rtx-5060/), which costs a bit more, avoids the overhead problem and has DLSS 4, but only 8 GB. The step-up is the [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/) at roughly $100 more, with 16 GB and a full x16 link. Buy the B580 for a new build around a Ryzen 5 7600 or Core Ultra 5; for an old-platform upgrade, look elsewhere.

description: The RX 6600 is a 2021 budget card for 1080p at $180 to $230 where still sold new: 8 GB, 132 W and solid raster speed, but no FSR 4 and weaker ray tracing.

verdict: The RX 6600 is a previous-generation 1080p card that still makes sense at the very bottom of the market. It launched in 2021 with 28 RDNA 2 compute units, 8 GB of GDDR6 and a 132 W rating, and independent reviews placed it roughly level with the RTX 3060 in raster games. Today that means medium to high settings at 1080p in most games and high frame rates in esports titles.

The catch is age. Availability varies: new stock is thin, and much of the supply is used or clearance at $180 to $230. Ray tracing is weak, and AMD launched FSR 4 as an RX 9000 feature, so this card relies on FSR 3. The 8 GB of VRAM forces lower textures in some new games, and the x8 link costs a little more on PCIe 3.0 boards when memory spills over. Late in 2025 AMD also moved RX 5000 and RX 6000 cards to a separate driver branch focused on fixes and game support rather than new features.

Buy one under $200, or used from a trusted seller, for an esports or older-game build. Once the price reaches the mid-$200s, the [Arc B580](/gear/arc-b580/) adds 12 GB of VRAM and XeSS 2 on a new card with a full warranty, and the [RTX 5060](/gear/rtx-5060/) is much faster with DLSS 4 for about $100 more. For new AAA games, the [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/) is the card worth saving for.

verdict: The RX 6700 XT is a previous-generation card whose 12 GB of VRAM keeps it relevant. It launched in 2021 with 40 RDNA 2 compute units on a 192-bit bus, and independent reviews placed it between the RTX 3060 Ti and RTX 3070 in raster games. That still means high settings at 1080p and playable 1440p in most games, without the texture limits that 8 GB cards hit.

Today it is mostly a used or clearance purchase at $250 to $330, and availability varies. The trade-offs are power and features. At 230 W it draws far more than newer cards of similar speed and needs a quality 650 W supply. Ray tracing is weak, and since AMD launched FSR 4 for RX 9000 cards, the 6700 XT relies on FSR 3. AMD also moved RX 6000 cards to a separate driver branch late in 2025, with new features going to newer Radeons first. Do not confuse it with the RX 6700 non-XT, which has 10 GB on a 160-bit bus and 36 compute units.

A used card near $250 is reasonable value for a 1440p raster build. New, the [Arc B580](/gear/arc-b580/) offers the same 12 GB with XeSS 2, a warranty and lower power for similar money, though it prefers a recent CPU. The better buy for most people is the [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/): 16 GB, FSR 4 and around 160 W for $350 to $400.

quick: The RTX 4060 has 3,072 CUDA cores and 8 GB of GDDR6 on a 128-bit bus. NVIDIA rates it at 115 W, and it runs on a PCIe 4.0 x8 link with DLSS frame generation.

verdict: The RTX 4060 is a previous-generation 1080p card that has been overtaken by its successor. It launched in 2023 with 3,072 CUDA cores, 8 GB of GDDR6 and a 115 W rating, and it introduced DLSS 3 frame generation at this price. It now supports the DLSS 4 upscaler too, though not Multi Frame Generation. It handles esports titles at high frame rates and most AAA games at 1080p medium to high settings.

The problem is the price next to the [RTX 5060](/gear/rtx-5060/). At $280 to $310 the 4060 sits only about $20 below the newer card, which independent reviews put around 20% faster, with GDDR7 and Multi Frame Generation. Both share the same 8 GB limit, which already forces lower textures in some new games, and both use an eight-lane link that costs more on PCIe 3.0 boards when memory spills over.

Its one real strength is efficiency. At 115 W it is one of the easiest cards to feed and cool, so it suits small builds and prebuilt upgrades with modest power supplies. Buy it only at a clear discount or used. Otherwise take the RTX 5060, or spend about $50 to $90 more on the [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/), which doubles the VRAM and is the better long-term card. The [Arc B580](/gear/arc-b580/) gives 12 GB for less with a recent CPU.

verdict: The RTX 4070 is a capable 1440p card that has been replaced by the [RTX 5070](/gear/rtx-5070/). It launched in 2023 with 5,888 CUDA cores and 12 GB of GDDR6X, and independent reviews placed it roughly level with the RTX 3080 at a much lower 200 W. It still runs most games at 1440p high settings, and DLSS frame generation helps in demanding titles. A later version with GDDR6 instead of GDDR6X also exists, so check the listing.

The issue is value. At $500 to $600 with stock thinning, it sits close to the RTX 5070, which independent reviews put around 20% faster and which adds GDDR7, PCIe 5.0 and Multi Frame Generation. Both have 12 GB, so neither gains a VRAM advantage, and both already need texture settings watched in a few new games at 1440p. The 4070's edge is power: at 200 W it runs cooler and quieter than the 250 W 5070, and many partner cards use a single 8-pin connector.

Buy it only when a clearance or used deal undercuts the RTX 5070 by $100 or more. Otherwise take the 5070, or the [RX 9070](/gear/rx-9070/) for 16 GB at a similar price. Owners of an RTX 4070 have little reason to move to a 5070; the [RTX 5070 Ti](/gear/rtx-5070-ti/) is the meaningful upgrade.
